# How to contribute {#sec-contributing .unnumbered}

This book is meant to be a working resource rather than a finished statement,
and it is short of the things only other people can supply. This page says what
would help most and how to send it.

## Four things the book is for

Four things, and a contribution is useful to the extent it serves one of them.

A record of why isoform-level resolution matters, argued from the primary
literature rather than asserted.

A catalogue of the best-established cases where a particular isoform of a gene
does a particular job, with the evidence that establishes it and the denominator
that bounds it.

A plain account of how isoforms are measured, including what each method assumes
and where those assumptions fail, so that a reader can judge a number rather
than only read it.

An argument that transcriptome studies should decide deliberately whether to
work at gene level, because the collapse to one number per gene is often
inherited rather than chosen.

## The contributions that would help most

**A chapter read by someone who knows the field.** No chapter has had this, and
it is the gap that matters more than all the others together. Every chapter
carries a first-draft notice saying so. A read that returns three real problems
is worth more to this project than a new section.

**A case the book is missing.** The book wants genes where an isoform difference
has a demonstrated specialised function, not merely a measured expression
difference. If a case you know is absent, naming the gene and one paper is
enough to act on.

**A correction.** Overstatement is the failure mode this project expects of
itself, because the automated checks compare numbers and wording and cannot see
a sentence that says slightly more than its source. Several such sentences have
been caught and fixed after publication. If a claim reads as stronger than the
paper behind it, say so and name the claim.

**An area that needs building out.** Some sections are thin because the subject
is thin, and others because the research pass stopped early. Pointing at a
section and saying which of those it is helps more than it sounds.

**Full text for a source read as an abstract.** A hundred and twenty of the
sources behind this book were read as abstracts rather than as full text, and
eighteen are cited as preprints that have not been through peer review. A
further twenty were read as preprints and are cited as the published versions
they later became, which no automated check can see. All three sets are counted
in `research/ALLOCATION.md`, with the commands that regenerate them. Telling the project that a preprint
now has a published version, or that a paywalled paper says something other than
its abstract implies, repairs a weakness the project already knows it has.

**A method the book explains badly.** The style guide commits this book to
explaining its own machinery completely, on the grounds that naming a method is
not explaining it. Where that promise is not kept, the gap is a defect and worth
reporting as one.

## Routes in, from an issue to a pull request

The low-effort route is an issue, and it is the preferred one for anything short
of a written section. Issue templates exist for a missing case, a correction and
an area to build out, at the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/brianjohnhaas/IsoformBiology/issues/new/choose).
A plain issue is equally welcome if none of them fits.

A pull request is welcome too, and it has one unusual requirement worth knowing
before you start. Prose in this book is not written from papers directly.
Reading a paper produces a claim record instead, holding the finding in the
reader's own words, the source, the exact lines read, and a short verbatim quote
kept only as an audit trail. A later writing pass then works from those records
rather than from source text. That separation is what makes close paraphrase
structurally unlikely instead of a matter of individual care, and it is why
every sentence can be traced to the lines behind it.

The full contract is in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/brianjohnhaas/IsoformBiology/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md),
along with the record schema, the automated checks that run on every push and an
explicit list of the things those checks cannot see. A contribution that adds
prose without adding records will fail the checks, which is the intended
behaviour rather than an obstacle to work around.

Corrections to prose alone, where no new source is involved, need none of that
machinery.

## Deliberately out of scope

It does not catalogue software, benchmark tools or teach pipelines. That work is
done well elsewhere and duplicating it would both waste effort and date the book
quickly. The glossary lists resources that do it properly. Where methods appear,
the unit is an approach and what it assumes, and an implementation is named only
as an example of one.

It also does not aim at completeness. A case earns its place by having evidence
behind it that a reader can check, so a well-evidenced small set is the goal
rather than a long list.
